pool.text: Rwanda and Burundi were assigned to Germany by the Berlin Conference.
Richard Kandt founded the city of Kigali as a German administrative outpost.
Belgian forces captured Kigali during World War I under Colonel Philippe Molitor.
Kigali officially became the national capital of Rwanda upon gaining independence.
Minister of defence Juvénal Habyarimana overthrew ruling president Grégoire Kayibanda.
President Juvénal Habyarimana was killed when his aircraft was shot down near Kigali.
The rebel Rwandan Patriotic Front successfully seized control of the city of Kigali.
The current boundaries of Kigali city were officially established through a new law.
Informal settlements in lower Kiyovu were expropriated by the government for new developments.
The Rwanda Stock Exchange officially launched financial services operations within the country.
The Kigali Up music festival began holding its annual events in July or August.
The local economy was reported to be dependent on foreign aid and resource extraction.
A World Bank study used night-light output to measure relative GDP across three districts.
An extraordinary summit of the African Union was hosted at new facilities in the city.
A new specialist hospital opened in the Nyarugenge district to handle specific medical treatments.
The official population of Kigali city reached 1,745,555 inhabitants according to records.
The Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting was held with high-profile international attendees.
The inaugural Kigali Cine Junction film festival took place across local public spaces.
The Rwanda asylum plan agreement with the United Kingdom was cancelled.
